transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’ve been feeling like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day, I’ll start with the garden club list, then end up at my knitting bag, then looking at travel papers… and I haven’t really finished any of it.
Since you were a child, have you usually had trouble staying focused and finishing tasks?

Yes… I think so. Even in grade school, teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but… scattered. I’d lose papers, talk before I was supposed to, and I remember having trouble sitting still long enough to finish my work.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or irritable?
I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve had anything like that, really. I can get annoyed, but not unusually high or anything.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?
Not really… I mean, I worry about normal things, I suppose. But I wouldn’t say it’s a lot for no reason.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with persistent symptoms since childhood, including distractibility, difficulty finishing tasks, losing papers, talking out of turn, and trouble sitting still. Symptoms appear chronic rather than episodic, and the patient denied features suggestive of mania and generalized anxiety as primary explanations.
